Subject: Volume tiers & SKU mapping — hosted → Dedicated → Private

Hi Erin —

Thanks for the chat earlier. Per your request, I attached a simple volume model (novus-volume-model.xlsx) and a one-page SKU mapping (hosted-dedicated-private-sku-mapping.pdf) that lays out how our commercial units translate across deployment modes.

A few quick clarifying questions so we can make the matrix actionable:
- Expected monthly token volume (avg + peak) for the first 12 months?
- Do you expect steady growth (linear) or step changes tied to feature launches?
- Which latency SLO matters most for the features in-scope (99th percentile ms)?
- Any mandatory compliance checklist items beyond SOC 2 and standard DPA?

What I included in the sheet: a per-tier hosted baseline (tokens/minute and per-token unit), equivalent Dedicated sizing assumptions (reserved GPU hours + expected sustained throughput) and an entry for Private (platform license + infra + support). The intention is to make it easy to compare marginal unit economics and one-time/setup items.

If this looks ok I’ll ask Sales Ops to produce a first-pass discount matrix and committed capacity options for you.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Volume tiers & SKU mapping — hosted → Dedicated → Private

Hi Marcus —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. I skimmed both and this looks like the right level. To answer your questions:
- Ballpark monthly tokens (month 1): 300M tokens; steady-state month 6+: 1.2B tokens (spiky during marketing campaigns).
- Growth: we expect step increases aligned with product launches (not smooth linear).
- Latency: P95 < 500ms is required for the main UI flows; for background batch tasks higher latency is acceptable.
- Compliance: SOC 2 + HIPAA considerations (we handle PHI in some workflows) — will need an answer on Private deployment path and KMS options.

For procurement, please provide a single table that shows: hosted unit price by volume tier + committed discount levels; equivalent Dedicated monthly commit for the same throughput; and Private: initial platform/licensing fee plus estimated infra run-rate.

Can you loop in anyone on pricing who can convert your assumptions into a simple, single-page quote matrix? Procurement wants to see line items that map directly to our internal cost model.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call after you send the matrix.

—Erin
Director, Product Operations
Novus Health
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 14:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Volume tiers & SKU mapping — hosted → Dedicated → Private

Marcus / Aisha —

Draft summary for Novus (based on Marcus’ model and Erin’s guidance). Sending as a short bulleted matrix — I’ve attached a formatted PDF.

High-level assumptions:
- Month 1: 300M tokens; steady-state (month 6+): 1.2B tokens with campaign spikes up to ~2.0B in peak months.
- Production SLO target: P95 < 500ms for UI flows.
- HIPAA: Private deployment required for PHI-bearing flows; Hosted can be scoped for non-PHI only.

Suggested commercial mapping (estimates for discussion):
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): tiered per-token pricing
  - 0–500M: $0.0012 / token
  - 500M–1.5B: $0.00095 / token
  - 1.5B+: custom enterprise tier (negotiated)
  - Setup: none; instant provisioning; included support (standard)

- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly commitment (GPU pool) + per-request routing
  - Equivalent to hosted 1.2B steady: recommended 4x A100-like reserved GPUs (configurable)
  - Monthly commit: $78,000 / month (includes reserved capacity + priority support)
  - Committed discounts: 10% for 12-month, 18% for 24-month
  - Setup: one-time provisioning fee: $12,000 (estimated)

- Private (customer-managed infra or on-prem): platform license + infra + support
  - Platform license: $95,000 one-time (enterprise package)
  - Professional services (deployment & hardening): $28,000 (one-time)
  - Ongoing support & maintenance: $9,500 / month
  - Infra run-rate: depends on sizing; estimate shown in attached sheet (we used 4x A100 equivalent)

Discounting guidance (internal):
- Small pilots (<= 3 months): limited or no discount on hosted; focus on usage credits.
- Annual committed Dedicated: match percentage discounts above; consider SLO-based credits only after contract signing.
- Private: most commercial levers are platform/license + PS; keep platform list above but be prepared to negotiate (especially for multi-year support).

Open items before we send to Novus:
- Confirm exact token definition (generation vs embeddings vs reranking). Pricing above assumes generation tokens only.
- Confirm whether HIPAA scope requires Private for the entire product or just a subset of flows.
- Legal: need to confirm standard DPA + HIPAA addendum route — looping in Lauren.

If this looks ok, I recommend we send a single-page customer-facing matrix and the workbook as backup. I can convert to a one-pager for procurement.

—Monica
Sales Operations — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Volume tiers & SKU mapping — hosted → Dedicated → Private

Erin —

Thanks for the details. Attaching the requested one-page matrix and the workbook we used to estimate run-rates (novus-volume-model.xlsx). Below is a short executive summary to make procurement mapping easier.

Executive summary (estimates):
- Hosted (fastest path): for your expected steady-state (1.2B tokens) the blended hosted unit price would be ~ $0.00095/token (see tiers). No setup fee. Good for quick launch of non-PHI features.
- Dedicated (predictable throughput): to cover the P95 < 500ms target and campaign spikes we recommend a reserved pool equivalent to 4x A100 GPUs. Estimated committed price: $78k/month before discount. 12/24 month discounts available (10% / 18%).
- Private (PHI / HIPAA path): platform license (one-time) + PS + support. Platform license and PS cover the on-prem/VPC control plane and KMS integration. Infra run-rate is variable; workbook includes a model using 4x A100 equivalent and sample cost ranges.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm which features must be HIPAA-bound (Private path) vs which can run on Hosted.
2) If Novus wants a firm Dedicated quote, Monica can convert the estimate to a formal commercial proposal with line items and optional tiers.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up this week to walk procurement through the one-pager.

Available times: Thu 10:00–11:30am PT, Fri 1:00–4:00pm PT. Which works for you?

Best,
Marcus Lin
